rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology and Results sections; the authors develop a procedure (maximum/minimum system head curves, 4,000 daily random demand curves, SOLVER optimisation of fixed/variable-speed pump combinations) and apply it with their own model runs to a 127.7 ha citrus on-demand network in Valencia, reporting design discharges, energy consumption (Table 4, Fig. 14) and annual total pumping-station costs (Fig. 15).
rows.notes: The study is a design/optimisation exercise for dimensioning and regulating the pumping station of an on-demand network. It does not compare investment costs of on-demand networks with other delivery schedules, nor does it attribute higher investment to guaranteeing peak-period supply as its own finding; it only shows that dimensioning for the maximum discharge of generated demand curves (218-256 L/s) rather than Clement's discharge (166 L/s) increases reliability, and reports project-plus-energy costs for pump combinations. All results are model runs on design data (hydrant discharges, crop requirements, market pump prices) with no comparison against measurements from the real network, so under the rating rules they do not count as own evidence on the claim. No limitations of the cost result are stated; standard deviations are reported for discharge and energy distributions but not for the cost/investment result relevant to the claim.

notes: Full text appears complete (pp. 273-281). Study is a methodological paper with an unvalidated application example; figure contents are not available beyond captions and in-text descriptions.
